parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented universal-exposure measure (no facility/border/custody rule sourced), and visitor-facing law is supportive: gender identity protected in goods/services since 2015, hate-crime penalties since 2019, constitutional non-discrimination. But those protections have documented inconsistent implementation, and reporting is thin — most bias crimes go only to community organisations, implying unreliable police recourse. Social climate shows real hostility: politicians' hate speech during civil-code debates, death threats, Pride held under repeated anonymous warnings. That is tier-3 societal hostility with weak demonstrated remedy, not tier-1 state exposure. The 2015 LGBTQ-wide prevalence figures are dated and not trans-specific (rule 17: no weight). Border treatment, custody placement and visitor care access are unsourced open questions, not exposures. No documented acceptance-with-working-enforcement record for visitors pulls it below the 0.65 anchors. Absence of criminalisation does not anchor it higher given documented hostility plus unproven remedy.
